facts: The installed tree contains examples/gemm/example_gemm_persistent.py using driver.get_num_sms() and T.Persistent.
T.Persistent is implemented in src/ir.cc and tilelang/language/loop.py as a generic logical-tile loop.
T.atomic_add exists, but Split-K still needs a legal reduction design and the MetaX release notes require version-specific atomic review.
A1b FC2 currently scales each output row by routed_expert_weights in its per-output-tile epilogue.
Prior A1b profiler evidence reported no private spill; therefore H4 is a measured tradeoff, not a presumed win.

hypotheses.mechanism: Use native T.Persistent for FC2 while preserving logical tiles and arithmetic.
hypotheses.external_fact: Multiple official frameworks implement persistent grouped/matmul scheduling by limiting physical programs and iterating logical tiles.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: A1b FC2's large logical grid may reduce scheduling overhead or improve device-side tile traversal on C500.
hypotheses.static_review: Use only locally installed T.Persistent; no CUDA TMA or architecture constants.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: The mechanism took effect, but limiting FC2 to one physical CTA per SM removed latency hiding and regressed end-to-end time.

hypotheses.mechanism: Load one routed expert weight per FC2 row into a local fragment and broadcast in the epilogue.
hypotheses.external_fact: Fused MoE implementations reuse device metadata and fuse scaling/combine work.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: Explicit caching may remove repeated global load instructions if the current compiler does not hoist the scalar automatically.
hypotheses.static_review: Multiplication location, type and ordering remain unchanged.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Profiler confirmed fewer FC2 global-read instructions, but both end-to-end improvements remained below the strict 0.5% gate.

hypotheses.mechanism: Move route scaling from the FC2 output epilogue to the FC1 SwiGLU intermediate epilogue using linearity.
hypotheses.external_fact: MoE kernels fuse activation/scaling/combine work to remove repeated traffic and operations.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: Scaling a smaller intermediate tile count may remove repeated FC2 metadata loads and multiplies.
hypotheses.static_review: Official Large and Small correctness at unchanged tolerance must gate all timing.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Unchanged-tolerance correctness passed, but earlier FP16 scaling introduced private traffic in FC1 and caused an end-to-end regression.

hypotheses.mechanism: Move the FC2 A tile from fragment/register scope to shared memory.
hypotheses.external_fact: GEMM schedules trade register and shared-memory footprints against occupancy and cooperative reuse.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: The change may reduce register pressure/redundant loads, or may regress by consuming about 32 KiB shared memory per block; mcProfiler decides.
hypotheses.static_review: A1b had no measured private spill, so no benefit is assumed.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Both complete runs exceeded the mean/median gate, profiler showed a mechanism-consistent FC2 cycle/read-instruction reduction without private spill, and ABBA was stable.

hypotheses.mechanism: Split-K with atomic or workspace reduction.
hypotheses.external_fact: CK Tile exposes Split-K offsets; MetaX release notes describe version-dependent atomic limitations.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: A1b already has abundant FC2 MxN tiles and the fixed ABI has no reduction workspace.
hypotheses.static_review: Excluded unless later profiler evidence proves K-parallelism is necessary and a legal reduction is found.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: No legal reduction workspace exists in the fixed ABI; atomic reduction changes ordering and the measured FC2 grid already exposes abundant MxN parallelism.

hypotheses.external_fact: These systems alter packing, capacity, dropping, or communication.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: The official benchmark already supplies padded expert-stacked inputs and fixed routing semantics.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Would change official routing, padding, capacity, token-drop semantics, or communication workload.

hypotheses.external_fact: TensorRT-LLM reports a Blackwell FP4 low-token regime where dense expert execution can win.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: Current C500 workload, precision and required expert work are different.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Would change required expert work and precision and relies on an unrelated Blackwell FP4 regime.

hypotheses.external_fact: The referenced implementation is architecture-specific to Hopper/Blackwell CUDA.
hypotheses.engineering_inference: The current TileLang-MACA fork exposes no equivalent mechanism.
hypotheses.static_review: Excluded; only generic T.Persistent is used.

c500_measured_conclusion.reason: Installed TileLang-MACA exposes no TMA/WGMMA/warp-specialization equivalent; only generic T.Persistent was tested as H1.
